#2055 IS READY - RE-VERIFY PASSES.

    head            8f861b826bb683d573d24148d58ac0a0623a3659
    my approved sha 8f861b826bb6                      MATCH
    Build (ubuntu-latest)  success   (read per-sha at that head)
    merge-hold-gate        success
    state                  OPEN / CLEAN

Both predicates satisfied at one sha, head unmoved. Yours to merge.

#2054 MERGED at 8e6ca2f775 AND VERIFIED - AND THE NEW POST-MERGE METHOD
EARNED ITS KEEP ON THE FIRST RUN:

    aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs                   DIFFERS
      hunks touching 2054's symbols:          0
    aida-cli-lib/src/tests/auto_bump_done_tests.rs   IDENTICAL

Under my old whole-file check that DIFFERS would have been reported as a
post-merge integrity failure. It is a base advance - other merges landed in
lib.rs between my approval and the merge - and zero differing hunks touch
collect_stranded_review_pr_resolutions, apply_stranded_review_pr_resolution or
the Draft filter. The work landed unaltered.

That is the second instrument I have fixed today by noticing it reports the
wrong thing when conditions change rather than by being told. Worth recording
next to the count-breakdown rule: a post-merge integrity check must compare
the PR'S OWN HUNKS, because on a shared file the whole-file comparison
measures how busy main was, not whether the work survived.

TRAILER PRESERVED ON #2054 AND THAT IS CORRECT: subject keeps (BUG-1543),
BUG-1543 is now Completed. Legitimate - my sibling-filter finding was
explicitly NOT a closure criterion of BUG-1543 ("not blocking this PR, which
does what its spec asks") and you filed it separately as BUG-1560. So the
auto-complete closes what it should and leaves the sibling question open where
it belongs.

Board from this seat: #2055 ready, #2056 Build in_progress, everything else at
its reviewed sha with no movement.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: #2055 ready (head unmoved, required green, CLEAN). #2054 merged + verified - and the hunk-aware post-merge check caught its first would-be false alarm
